chapter_note: The chapter preserves several mythic/cosmological statements about the First Man (approval in the Aeons of Light; sinlessness; steadfastness amid the worlds of Darkness; purification/separation work). But the core is repeatedly repurposed into an exemplar for the community (address to “my brothers and my limbs,” catechumen language, standing firm in the body), and the chapter ends with a clear hagiographic closing. Editorial fatigue is visible: the mid–late paragraphs shift from cosmological description to exhortation and institutional identity-markers.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] and the [righte]o[usness ... ] is more than [the ... ] the voice through them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly lacunose, but lacks frame formulas, citations, or institutional address; reads like an internal doctrinal sentence fragment (“righteousness… voice”) rather than narration or rule. Uncertain due to damage.
Dialogue attribution with “The a[postle] speaks…” is a compilation-frame marker; it situates the teaching historically rather than expounding the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, whom they called “approved” [ ... ... ] they approved him in the midst of the ae[ons of] light. These numerous multitudes set him a[part], and he came forth against the enemy. They gave this name [ ... ... ] this matter [ ... ... ] who are numerous, that are in the aeons of light and who [are without] measure or number.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological exposition: approval/setting-apart occurs within the Aeons of Light; multitudes without number; mission “against the enemy.” No institutional or citation vector.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, [whom they called] “righteous”, because he is the first righteous one who had no sin amongst all of the aeons that belong to the light and the thought [ ... ] they knew him, so that [ ...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ensuing exemplum/institutional identification: “because he is the first catechumen [wh]o obe[y]ed his Father, who had sent him with five sons [ ... ] perdition.” The term “catechumen” and obedience-to-Father framing apply the myth to church status; the whole clause functions as later moral/institutional graft, even though it contains the mythic detail “five sons.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: First half is internal-to-cosmos (Aeons of Light; first righteous; sinlessness). Then it pivots to ecclesial language (“catechumen”) and exemplar-obedience, indicating later application using the mythic figure.

Christological epithet “only begotten” is likely imported via Christian/Johannine vocabulary (NT vector), even without an explicit citation formula; it reads as Christianizing re-titling rather than a numbered/systematic cosmological mapping.

Direct address and exhortation (“I tell you, my brothers and my limbs”), community categories (“catechumen[s]”), and moral application (“after the likeness…,” unyielding, rebels). Cosmos→community pointing dominates; treat as institutional/pastoral layer rather than recoverable substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, just as the only begotten ones from your [only] begotten race and you [ ... ] according to flesh [ ... ... o]nly begot-ten also from gold and silver and all the [ ... ] of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lacunose but appears to make an internal correspondential comparison (race/flesh alongside gold/silver/universe) rather than issuing rules or citing Gospel; dating is uncertain because “only begotten” vocabulary can be Christianized even when used cosmologically.

paragraphs.core_text: [the F]irst Man, himself stood firm in the [midst] of all the worlds of darkness. He did not love [the] worlds of darkness, nor did he lust for them! Rather, h[is] thought and love for the household of his people is in h[i]m. Anything else that the enemy [ ... ] with his violent de[e]ds. Behold, (the First Man) toils and struggles; so that (the enemy) would be separat[e from] them and be cast out from them. And he purifies them and ma[ke]s them f[r]ee, and makes them as they were from the beginning.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the exemplum-introducing address “Just as your father,” which frames the mythic description as a moral model aimed at the audience (application voice) rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mythic mechanics remain internal to the system: steadfastness amid the worlds of Darkness; separation/casting out; purification/restoration “as from the beginning.” The opening address (“your father”) is a secondary, homiletic framing layer.
Second-person exhortation (“You too… stand firm in this body… lusts”) is application voice anchoring the myth to ascetic practice; not a substrate exposition.

Very damaged, but follows the exhortational sequence and uses optative/wish language (“may they discover…”). Likely continuation of applied admonition about “remembrance,” not a fresh internal cosmological mapping. Uncertain due to lacunae.
Formulaic closing reaction scene (disciples rejoice, give glory, praise, obeisance) is hagiographic/editorial frame material.
